- If sentiment is negative or shows recent downward momentum, reduce forecasted price targets, especially in the first 10 days of the 30-day horizon.  
- If sentiment is positive and forecast shows a sharp spike, cap the overshoot at +10% above the 14-day moving average to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment has recently turned positive (e.g., >0.25), model tends to overestimate; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to the first 7 days of forecast.  
- If history shows strong mean reversion (e.g., recent price drops followed by recovery), model often overcorrects; reduce forecast peak by 5–15% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.  
- If sentiment is flat or negative, model tends to underpredict; increase forecast by 3–8% in the first 5 days if recent price is trending down.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp upward moves when sentiment is mixed or recently negative — cap upward momentum at 5% above prior 7-day average.
